## 固定收益開篇主論述

美國公債在7月最後一個交易日再度全面遭到拋售。勞動成本數據穩健、聯準會異議官員日益明確要求升息，加上油價重新上漲，迫使投資人同時反映近期政策需進一步收緊，以及長期通膨溢價擴大的風險。2年期殖利率上升4.5個基點至4.292%，5年期與10年期均上升6.2個基點，分別報4.45%與4.736%；30年期上升5.9個基點至5.274%。30年期盤中最高觸及5.28%，續創2007年以來新高；10年期盤中突破4.74%，為2025年1月以來首次。

這次走勢不及本週稍早聯準會會議後的熊市陡峭化劇烈，卻更難歸因於單一券期重新定價。2年期與10年期利差擴大1.7個基點至44.4個基點，2年期與30年期利差擴大1.4個基點至98.2個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升3.6個基點至2.45%，損益兩平通膨率增加2.6個基點至2.286%，顯示通膨補償與經通膨調整後的折現率，對名目殖利率升幅的貢獻幾乎相當。

這種組合有別於前一交易日的局部回穩。第2季就業成本指數上升0.9%，略高於經濟學家預期；3位具投票權的地區聯準銀行總裁也說明，為何他們在7月會議主張立即升息。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack認為政策限制性不足；明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari傾向在官員蒐集更多資訊期間逐步緊縮；達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan則警告，近期採取溫和行動，可降低日後被迫大幅緊縮的需要。里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin另稱，現行政策設定是否足夠緊縮是相當接近的判斷；今年沒有投票權的聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem則表示，他也會傾向升息1碼。

油價進一步強化這項訊息。從波斯灣到黑海的供給威脅仍未解除，WTI上漲1.29%至$84.67，Brent上漲1.22%至$90.12。單日漲幅雖然溫和，但WTI全月已上漲21.83%，Brent上漲23.59%，使聯準會、歐洲央行與英國央行必須判斷，暫時性的能源壓力是否正轉化為更持久的價格衝擊。

美國公債下跌之際，股市反而上漲，並非風險資產遭到全面清算。S&P 500上漲0.70%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.60%；費城半導體指數則幾乎持平，7月累計下跌20.61%。即使美國殖利率走高，美元指數仍下跌0.21%，全週跌幅達1.65%；黃金下跌1.24%至$4,049.10。不同資產走勢分歧，並未改變市場的核心問題：投資人仍願意選擇性支持風險資產，但在聯準會政策框架不明之際，若要為經濟提供長天期融資，他們要求更高補償。

## 實質殖利率與通膨補償推動美國公債拋售

週五殖利率再度上升，為存續期間部位備受壓力的7月劃下句點。7月全月，2年期殖利率上升11.7個基點、5年期上升22.3個基點、10年期上升27個基點、30年期上升32.1個基點；2年期與30年期利差擴大20.4個基點，顯示這次調整遠不只反映下一次升息時點。

10年期實質殖利率占名目基準殖利率全月升幅的22.4個基點。同期間損益兩平通膨率僅上升4.6個基點，但隨油價於週五反彈，且政策官員強調通膨可能持續高於目標，其影響變得更加重要。實質資金成本與投資人要求的未來通膨補償因而同步上升，並非兩者之間單純此消彼長。

債券指數表現顯示，各券期均受到影響。ICE美國政府1至3年期債券指數週五下跌0.04%，7月仍上漲0.17%；7至10年期指數單日下跌0.31%、全月下跌1.17%；20年以上指數週五下跌0.69%，7月跌幅達3.87%。長天期高評級公司債指數全月下跌超過4%，主要反映政府債券殖利率上升帶來的存續期間曝險。

月底交易活動異常熱絡。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量達$1.92兆，較週四增加32.4%，共計577,862筆交易。名目附息債交易量增加33.4%至$1.52兆；超過7年至10年期券種的交易量增加56.4%至$2,790億，超過5年至7年期券種的成交額增加88.5%至$1,730億；TIPS交易量則接近3倍，達$1,212億。這些數據呈現調整的規模與集中區域，但無法判定由市場哪一方發動。

尾盤出現一股抵銷力量。紐約時間下午4時債券指數進行再平衡，追蹤指數的基金納入7月新發債券，美國公債跌幅因而收斂，但這項需求並未扭轉單日拋售或全月跌勢。截至前一交易日，彭博美國公債指數7月已下跌近0.9%，聯準會決策與稍早油價推動的重新定價，是全月最主要的兩次衝擊。

就業成本指數帶來一項有別於能源的國內通膨疑慮。該指數季增0.9%，高於預測中位數，顯示勞動成本放緩程度仍不足以安撫原已質疑政策利率是否具有限制性的市場。單憑這項數據尚不能確認勞動成本正在加速，但在週五的市場環境下，即使只是略高於預期，也足以產生明顯影響。利率交易員Tony Farren指出，市場需要看到通膨下降的證據，而不是另一項僅略強於預期的數據。

油價隨後使市場面臨的可能情境更加分歧。美國與伊朗戰事再起，區域航運又面臨威脅，供給風險居高不下，WTI收於$84之上，創一週新高。油價上漲直接影響長天期債券；在供給衝擊接連出現之際，投資人原已要求更高補償，以防通膨持續。

跨資產反應顯示，殖利率上升並非單純源於風險偏好轉強。Amazon等大型科技公司帶動S&P 500盤中一度上漲近1%，終場收高0.70%；但半導體指數幾乎沒有上漲，全週仍下跌4.30%，7月跌幅超過20%。投資人仍明顯區分有能力為AI建設提供資金的企業，以及對槓桿、產能擴張或擁擠部位最為敏感的公司。

美元走弱更不尋常。儘管美國公債殖利率上升，彭博廣泛美元指數全週仍下跌1.3%，創3個多月來最差表現。聯準會會議前，市場部位已高度偏多美元：截至7月28日，非商業交易者持有$492.3億美元淨多單，為2014年以來最大。美元隨後下跌，既反映日圓干預，也反映市場擔心聯準會仰賴市場自行收緊金融情勢，可能不足以控制通膨。

## 聯準會異議官員補上主席未明示的反應函數

7月會議的3位異議官員，提供了本週最清楚的政策指引。Hammack、Kashkari與Logan均投票主張將聯邦基金利率目標從3.5%至3.75%的區間向上調整，而非連續第5次會議維持不變。他們週五的發言顯示，3人對政策方向看法一致，但在理由與著重之處仍有重要差異。

Hammack表示，通膨居高不下的時間已過久，現行政策的限制程度並不適當。她不確信若不採取額外行動，通膨能回到2%，並認為推升價格的不只有供給衝擊，也包括需求壓力。她將經濟的基礎韌性視為及早行動的理由，因為此時採取措施的代價仍可控制。

Kashkari傾向連續採取小幅升息，而非等到通膨根深蒂固後才進行更大幅度的干預。他認為，如果通膨回落，聯準會可放慢或暫停後續調整，既保留彈性，也降低持續延後行動導致較高通膨預期獲得強化的風險。這種主張是把每次調整的幅度與前景不確定性相連，而非代表其緊縮決心較弱。

Logan表示，即使考慮生產力改善與供給干擾，通膨看來也只是朝2%區間中段移動，而非一路回到聯準會目標。她以就業、支出與金融情勢保持穩健為據，認為政策並未實質抑制需求。在她看來，近期溫和升息可降低日後必須更突然收緊政策的機率。

目前沒有投票權的Musalem補充指出，債券市場遭到拋售，使聯準會信譽取決於更高利率；他原會傾向升息1碼。同樣在今年沒有投票權的Barkin並未直接支持異議官員，但表示現行利率是否高到足以壓低通膨，是相當接近的判斷；他認為有理由收回2025年的部分降息。

這些發言改變了政策辯論，因為它們來自在不同時點公開表態的具名官員，而非一個匿名的緊縮派陣營。此前，主席Kevin Warsh拒絕明確說明何種條件會觸發行動。Warsh主張，市場殖利率上升已在收緊金融情勢，可替央行完成部分工作；異議官員則強調，若沒有政策配合，僅靠市場收緊未必能使通膨回到目標。

這項差異對長端尤其重要。若殖利率上升源於市場相信通膨終將下降，金融情勢會收緊，聯準會信譽也可維持；若升勢來自期限溢價、通膨預期或央行反應的不確定性，借款成本雖會提高，卻無法提供同等的政策錨定效果。週五實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率對升幅的貢獻相當，美元又同步走弱，因此市場仍有理由採取後一種解讀。

Warsh的溝通策略本身也日益成為溢價來源。他試圖減少前瞻指引、縮短政策聲明，並成立工作小組重新檢討溝通、經濟數據與資產負債表政策。投資人過去習慣依據聯準會明示的反應函數為未來會議定價，如今卻必須從數據與市場走勢推斷，而這些變化本身的成因可能並不明確。

週末又浮現一項制度變革構想。Warsh在7月會議提出，可能把每年設定利率的會議減至6次，另安排2次會議討論實質經濟議題。FOMC自1980年代初以來，每年均舉行8次例行政策會議，目前尚未作成決定；官員也討論了讓決策時點與主要數據發布更緊密配合。

改變會議頻率不會妨礙聯準會在緊急情況下開會，但預定決策次數減少，可能提高每輪數據的重要性，並拉長市場在沒有政策回應下運作的時間。這項提議符合Warsh改革央行溝通方式的整體方向，卻也出現在指引不足已提高市場對大幅殖利率波動避險需求之際。

選擇權市場已反映這項疑慮。長天期美國公債期貨的賣權相對買權溢價升至3月以來最高。投資人利用9月選擇權，對沖10年期殖利率接近4.8%或4.9%，以及30年期殖利率升至約5.3%至5.42%的風險。聯準會會議後以約$2,000萬買進的一筆長債賣權部位，隨30年期殖利率逼近其履約區域，價值已大幅上升。

美國財政部的季度再融資計畫帶來另一項不確定性。市場預期8月至10月一季的標售規模維持穩定，但投資人留意任何為2027年擴大發債預作準備的指引。30年期殖利率已高於5.27%；即使聯準會下一步變得更清楚，若財政部暗示未來附息債供給增加，仍可能進一步推升期限溢價。

財政部也在研究調整融資市場操作的可能性。官員詢問主要交易商，是否可將部分政府現金投入規模約$13兆的附買回市場。財政部在聯準會帳戶中持有約$9,660億，整體現金餘額接近$1兆；透過附買回交易貸出部分資金，可望平滑繳稅日、標售交割與現金餘額變動對短期融資市場的影響。

支持者認為，這項計畫可以減輕週期性壓力，並讓聯準會以略小的資產負債表運作。財政部借款諮詢委員則較不認同，5月時判斷操作困難可能超過有限收益。在銀行準備金充裕時，預估收益介於0至2個基點；準備金較稀缺時則為5至10個基點。交易商承作能力也是限制：規模龐大且不定期的財政部附買回操作可能占用中介機構的資產負債表，但業者無法無限期保留閒置空間以備需求。

## 日本央行按兵不動，協調干預改變日圓風險

日本央行按兵不動之際，日本也展開非比尋常的匯市操作。日本央行將基準利率維持在1%，符合受訪52位經濟學家全數預期；該行6月才將利率調升至1995年以來最高。決議以8比1通過，高田創尋求連續第2次升息。

總裁植田和男的訊息溫和偏鷹，但未承諾9月採取行動。他表示，基礎通膨正接近2%目標，因此必須更加留意上行風險；政策委員會將在下次會議展開更深入的政策討論。若日本央行認定金融情勢過度寬鬆，也可能加快升息步伐。

更新後的展望使未來各次會議仍保有行動可能。日本央行把經濟成長風險評估由偏向下行改為大致平衡，並預測本會計年度經濟成長0.6%。政府補貼促使主要通膨預測由2.8%下修至2.5%，但央行同時警告，基礎通膨可能超過2%，日圓疲弱也已成為更重要的價格壓力來源。

決策前公布的數據加深了這項疑慮。東京7月不含生鮮食品的消費者物價年增1.9%，高於1.8%的預測；不含生鮮食品與能源的通膨率及整體通膨率均為2%。加工食品價格上漲3.9%，家事用品上漲5.3%，服務通膨則小幅升至1.2%。6月工業生產月增1.3%、年增4.2%；零售銷售年增0.5%，但月減4.1%。失業率維持2.5%，求才求職比則由1.17升至1.18。

然而，政策訊息的力道不足以延續日圓最初由干預帶動的急升。據市場人士表示，日本進場後，日圓兌美元在週四紐約交易時段一度升值3.3%。日本央行帳戶預估顯示，此次操作規模約為¥8.45兆，折合$528億，可能是東京歷來規模最大的單日干預。

這項估算來自日本央行週一經常帳餘額預計因財政相關因素減少¥8.2兆，與貨幣經紀商原先預期增加形成落差。財務省未立即證實干預，但這項差異使進場操作的可能性極高。美國當局也進行匯率詢價，財政部長Scott Bessent形容日圓被嚴重低估，過度波動並不健康。

行動延續至週五紐約交易時段。知情人士表示，日本當局再次買進日圓、賣出美元。紐約聯準銀行要求至少2家美國大型銀行對歐元兌日圓進行詢價；另有報導指出，紐約聯準銀行代表美國財政部賣出歐元、買進日圓。日圓週五兌美元升值約1.3%，收在157.28附近，僅用2個交易日便扭轉逾2個月的貶勢。

操作規模及美日雙邊參與，改變了日圓空頭部位的近期風險。截至7月28日，避險基金持有124,575口看空日圓合約，價值約$95億，接近6月高峰，也是2007年以來最大空頭曝險。官方干預不僅直接買進日圓，也帶來華府可能支持進一步行動的前景，使這些擁擠部位正面承受壓力。

長期限制仍是利差。日本1%的政策利率遠低於美國利率區間3.75%的上限。植田和男雖為緊縮留下可能，卻未承諾升息；交易員定價顯示，10月前升息的機率約為89%。日本央行下次決策訂於9月18日，較聯準會預定會議晚2天。

協調行動在週末正式升級。日本證實與美國進行15年來首次聯合干預；美國總統Donald Trump稱此舉是友誼的象徵，Bessent則表示，華府如有必要將毫不猶豫再次干預。財政部長面前一張被拍攝到的便條，列出買進$50億至$100億日圓的計畫。這些證實均發生在週五固定收益市場收盤後，因此沒有推動當日美國公債走勢，但也提高了日圓一旦再次貶值，可能遭遇更多官方抵抗的機率。

協調干預可以爭取時間，卻無法消除日圓疲弱背後的貨幣政策與財政因素。油價上漲加重日本的進口負擔，政府支出計畫也引發債券供給增加的疑慮。干預還可能迫使日本出售包括美國公債在內的外國證券，進而外溢至美國借款成本。日圓反彈能否持久，仍取決於日本央行緊縮、聯準會政策與日本財政展望是否開始為官方操作提供支撐。

## 歐洲通膨升溫與哥倫比亞暫停升息，擴大政策分歧

歐元區通膨率由6月的2.8%升至7月的2.9%，符合預測中位數，但進一步支持歐洲央行再次升息。能源價格年增10%，服務通膨及不含食品與能源的通膨指標也同步加速。德國公債回吐稍早漲幅，10年期殖利率上升1個基點至3.16%。

法國帶來各國數據中最大的意外。通膨率由2%躍升至2.4%，高於調查中的所有預測；服務通膨由1.9%升至2.3%，能源通膨達12.4%。在此之前，法國產出已強於預期，西班牙與德國通膨也出現類似加速，因而削弱了能源衝擊可由疲弱需求抵銷的論點。

市場仍認為歐洲央行9月升息1碼的機率約為90%，並反映年底前累計緊縮42個基點。奧地利央行總裁Martin Kocher強調目前的不確定性異常偏高；立陶宛央行總裁Gediminas Simkus表示，升息的可能性遠高於按兵不動；斯洛伐克央行總裁Peter Kazimir則認為，即使情勢改善，仍至少需要再升息一次。

歐洲央行作成決策前，還將取得8月通膨數據與新的幕僚預測。7月報告已顯示，能源衝擊的範圍足以同時推高整體與基礎通膨指標，但其傳導會持續多久仍未確定。歐洲央行一項調查顯示，薪資成長預計將一路加速至2027年初；第2季經濟成長幅度則達預測的2倍，且為逾一年來最快。

英國方面，英國央行首席經濟學家Huw Pill在與另外2位委員投票支持升息後，進一步闡述鷹派立場。他警告，由於伊朗衝突的持續時間與規模高度不確定，能源與大宗商品價格波動可能延續至2027年。英國央行的基準預測顯示，年底通膨率為3.2%；若能源成本更高並出現第二輪效應，逆境情境下2027年通膨可達4.5%，利率也會明顯高於目前的3.75%。

Pill擔心的不只是燃料價格的第一輪漲勢。英國汽油價格已升至每公升159.97便士，較戰前高20%；政策分歧的核心在於企業是否會調高售價，以及勞工是否會要求薪資補償。總裁Andrew Bailey與另外5位貨幣政策委員認為，疲弱需求與勞動市場疲軟將限制這種傳導。Pill則主張，政策應在影響形成自我延續前加以阻止，而非等到現象明顯後才行動；不過，他也承認通膨預期尚未顯著脫離錨定。

面對高於目標的通膨，哥倫比亞採取了不同做法。央行意外將政策利率維持在12%；27位受訪經濟學家中僅4位預測按兵不動，其餘均預期升息25至75個基點。4位理事支持維持利率，3位則主張升息2碼。

央行總裁Leonardo Villar將這次決定形容為暫停，而非緊縮週期結束。相較於3%的目標及上下1個百分點的容忍區間，年通膨率仍高於6%；但哥倫比亞披索今年兌美元已升值近20%，減輕了進口價格壓力。央行也宣布最多增持$40億外匯存底的計畫，可能抑制披索升勢。

政策環境在政治與財政層面仍相當棘手。擴張性政府支出、最低工資上調23%，以及暫時性的食品與能源衝擊，都在助長通膨。獨立財政委員會預計，預算赤字將超過GDP的7%。Villar表示仍可能升息；總統當選人Abelardo de la Espriella將於8月7日就職，9月會議屆時也會有一位新任財政部長參與。

## 信用壓力區分存續期間損失與個別借款人風險

即使發行人信用並未普遍惡化，政府債券殖利率上升仍持續壓抑市政債。截至週四，彭博市政債券指數已下跌1.72%，創2003年以來最差7月表現，也是今年僅第2個下跌月份。7月通常可受惠於供給減少，以及票息與到期贖回資金再投資，但本月發行量約達$470億。

大量發行與美國公債殖利率上升這項罕見組合，壓過了季節性支撐。市政債相對美國公債因而變得便宜，但投資組合經理認為，這主要源於高利率環境，而非州與地方政府財務惡化。這項區別不會消除存續期間損失，卻顯示重新定價是全市場資金成本調整，而非廣泛信用事件的跡象。

紐約市凸顯了短期融資管道仍暢通與中期財政路徑惡化之間的差異。在該市計畫發行$15億債券前，Fitch與Moody’s均維持評等不變，但繼續將其$530億一般責任債列為負向展望。Moody’s評為Aa2，Fitch評為AA。

紐約市在未動用準備金或調高房產稅的情況下，使$1,260億預算達成收支平衡，主因截至6月的會計年度稅收較預測高出$43億。然而，支出計畫仍比前一年增加$100億，且仰賴延長退休金債務付款期程及增加州政府支持等暫時措施。預估赤字將擴大至2028會計年度的$64億及2030年的$85億。評等機構表示，能否持續採取措施彌補缺口，將決定未來一年評等能否維持。

Northwell Healthcare可能再為紐約市政債發行管線增加最多$8億供給。該醫療體系預計透過紐約州宿舍管理局發行免稅債券，由Jefferies擔任簿記管理人，但結構、期限與時點尚未確定。今年以來，醫院已發行約$267億市政債。

低品質企業資本結構面臨的壓力更為嚴重。隨著寬頻業者Cable One的債務遭到拋售，約$10億新融資受到威脅，債權人已開始組織協商。私募股權業者GTCR行使賣回權後，Cable One必須收購Mega Broadband Investments剩餘55%股權，因此需要這筆資金。

融資討論聚焦於接近12%的殖利率，已屬今年交易中最高水準之一。潛在貸款人要求嚴格進行資產隔離，防止Cable One動用母公司資源支援債務負擔較重的Mega Broadband。隨Cable One既有債務進一步走弱，部分第一順位擔保貸款的交易殖利率逼近18%，新融資方案可能因成本過高而無法完成。截至3月31日，Cable One至少有$30億長期債務，同時面臨高槓桿、自由現金流受限，以及住宅寬頻市場競爭激烈等問題。

Extenet Systems則已從再融資壓力走到付款失敗。這家小型基地台營運商未能支付7月27日到期的資產擔保證券利息，使債券構成違約。負責收款的PNC Bank旗下Midland Loan Services另指稱，屬於債券持有人的資金被存入其他帳戶，部分擔保權也已不再維持完整效力。

Extenet已發行約$5億資產擔保證券，並於6月警告債權人，公司現金即將耗盡。Moody’s表示，Extenet正協商利息暫緩追索協議，Kroll則仍在要求取得資訊。現金管理相關指控使問題不再只是營運資金短缺，因為這也令人質疑原本用於保護證券化債權人的控制機制。

Cable One與Extenet呈現同一融資限制的兩個階段。Cable One仍可能取得融資，但面臨兩位數殖利率、資產隔離要求與相互競爭的債權人團體；Extenet已發生付息違約，並在被指違反交易文件之際協商暫緩追索。兩起事件都不足以證明信用市場全面關閉，卻顯示無風險利率上升與營運表現轉弱，如何暴露過去依賴廉價再融資的資本結構。

羅馬尼亞主權評等則是另一個融資管道仍在、但警訊未除的案例。在政府對Fitch最初決定提出申訴並補充資料後，Fitch確認其評等為BBB-，即最低投資等級，展望為負向。這項消息在週五美國市場收盤後公布，因此並未影響當日美國公債走勢。

羅馬尼亞今年財政赤字預計將由2024年超過GDP的9%，降至低於6%；但執政聯盟5月瓦解後，政府一直沒有國會多數席次。Fitch指出，下屆政府的組成與穩定性存在不確定性，2026年後的財政策略能見度也已降低。Moody’s預定於8月7日檢討評等，另有2項改革必須在8月底前獲得批准，才能取得更多歐盟復甦資金。

## 後續市場意義

8月7日公布的7月就業報告，是異議官員提出立即緊縮主張後，美國面臨的第一項重大考驗。經濟學家預計，非農就業人數將在6月增加57,000人後，再增85,000人，失業率維持4.2%。若數據較強，將支持現行政策對需求的限制仍不足以使通膨回到目標；若報告疲弱，則會重新引發疑問：當勞動需求失去動能時，聯準會是否仍應回應由能源帶動的通膨。

其他勞動市場指標將協助判斷強弱是否廣泛。職缺數據週二公布、ADP民間就業估計週三公布、初領失業救濟金人數則於週四出爐。堪薩斯市聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid、聯準會理事Lisa Cook及Musalem也將分別發表談話，可用來觀察支持異議官員的範圍，是否已超出7月主張升息的幾位官員。

財政部8月至10月的再融資公告，是一項獨立的長天期利率事件。市場預期標售規模維持不變，但焦點在官員是否繼續表示擴大標售仍很遙遠，或轉而弱化這項指引。目前10年期選擇權結構鎖定殖利率接近4.9%的風險，長債避險範圍則延伸至5.42%；即使就業數據釐清9月政策爭議，若官方提早暗示2027年供給將擴大，仍可能延續拋售。

聯準會溝通本身仍是波動來源。Warsh據報考慮把每年設定利率的會議減至6次，使通膨框架及市場殖利率在政策中的角色之外，又增加一項制度問題。無論是說明這項提議、安排依數據作成決策的時點，或界定9月升息條件，都會影響投資人在會議之間要求多少額外溢價。

日圓將檢驗協調干預若未立即獲得利差支持，能否持續奏效。聯準會9月16日決策與日本央行9月18日會議相隔僅2天，兩條政策路徑將接連接受檢驗。若日圓再次貶向觸發上週行動的價位，將考驗美日是否有決心再度干預；若匯率保持穩定，則可讓植田和男有更多空間評估通膨與6月升息的影響。

歐洲央行方面，8月通膨與幕僚預測必須協助判斷，7月能源成本上漲10%的影響是否正擴散至服務與薪資。法國通膨意外升至2.4%、歐元區通膨達2.9%，均支持9月升息，但官員仍須判斷，經濟成長吸收較高能源成本之際，衝擊能否持續。

信用市場方面，Cable One的融資條件將顯示，12%的殖利率加上可執行的資產隔離安排，是否仍能吸引足夠需求以完成強制收購。Extenet的暫緩追索協商，將檢驗債券持有人能否在付款違約後，恢復現金控管與擔保權保障。紐約市$15億發債則能更清楚衡量，市政債投資人如何區分偏高的美國公債殖利率與發行人中期預算風險。

油價是上述考驗的共同變數。若波斯灣航運再次中斷，或美國與伊朗戰事升級，將挑戰能源衝擊只是暫時現象的假設，強化聯準會與歐洲央行鷹派官員的論點，並使損益兩平通膨率維持高檔。航運與外交若能持久改善，可緩解通膨補償；但7月底收盤走勢顯示，在更廣泛的長天期溢價回落前，長天期美國公債還需要市場對實質利率政策、財政供給及央行反應函數恢復信心。

overall_summary.headline: 勞動成本、聯準會鷹派異議與油價推升實質殖利率及通膨補償，美國公債遭到拋售
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債在7月最後一個交易日全面遭到拋售。2年期殖利率上升4.5個基點至4.292%，5年期與10年期均上升6.2個基點，分別報4.45%與4.736%；30年期上升5.9個基點至5.274%。10年期實質殖利率上升3.6個基點，損益兩平通膨率增加2.6個基點，顯示實質借款成本與通膨補償對升勢的貢獻幾乎相當。

第2季就業成本指數上升0.9%，略高於預期；具投票權的聯準會官員Beth Hammack、Neel Kashkari與Lorie Logan也說明，為何他們在7月主張立即升息。尚未解除的供給威脅推升WTI與Brent，兩者月漲幅均超過20%，使油價進一步加深通膨疑慮。

債券下跌並非廣泛避險所致：S&P 500與Nasdaq 100上漲，美元則在美國殖利率走高之際轉弱。日本干預匯市及日本央行溫和偏鷹的利率決定，也改變了日圓風險；不過，美日龐大利差仍限制日圓反彈的持久性。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries ended July with another broad selloff as firm labor-cost data, increasingly explicit demands for higher rates from Federal Reserve dissenters and a renewed rise in oil prices forced investors to price both more near-term restraint and a larger long-term inflation premium. The 2-year yield rose 4.5 basis points to 4.292%, the 5-year and 10-year each climbed 6.2 basis points to 4.45% and 4.736%, and the 30-year increased 5.9 basis points to 5.274%. The long bond traded as high as 5.28%, extending its move to the highest level since 2007, while the 10-year exceeded 4.74% intraday for the first time since January 2025.

The composition was less extreme than the post-Fed bear steepening earlier in the week but more difficult to dismiss as a single segment’s repricing. The 2s10s curve widened 1.7 basis points to 44.4 basis points, and 2s30s increased 1.4 basis points to 98.2 basis points. At 10 years, the real yield rose 3.6 basis points to 2.45% and the breakeven inflation rate increased 2.6 basis points to 2.286%. Higher inflation compensation and a higher inflation-adjusted discount rate therefore contributed almost equally to the nominal move.

That combination distinguished Friday from the previous session’s partial stabilization. The Employment Cost Index rose 0.9% in the second quarter, slightly more than economists expected, while three voting regional Fed presidents explained why they had preferred an immediate rate increase at the July meeting. Cleveland’s Beth Hammack argued that policy was not sufficiently restrictive, Minneapolis’s Neel Kashkari favored incremental tightening while officials gathered more information, and Dallas’s Lorie Logan warned that modest action soon could reduce the need for sharper action later. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin separately described the adequacy of the existing policy setting as a close call, while nonvoting St. Louis President Alberto Musalem said he would also have preferred a quarter-point increase.

Oil reinforced that message. WTI gained 1.29% to $84.67 and Brent rose 1.22% to $90.12 as threats to supply from the Persian Gulf to the Black Sea remained unresolved. The one-day moves were moderate, but WTI had risen 21.83% over the month and Brent 23.59%, leaving the Fed, the European Central Bank and the Bank of England to judge whether temporary energy pressure was becoming a more persistent price shock.

The Treasury decline occurred alongside rising equities rather than a broad liquidation of risk. The S&P 500 gained 0.70% and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.60%, although the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was nearly unchanged and finished July down 20.61%. The dollar index declined 0.21% and lost 1.65% over the week even as U.S. yields rose, while gold fell 1.24% to $4,049.10. The divergence left the central issue intact: investors were willing to support risk assets selectively, but they demanded more compensation to finance the economy at long maturities while the Fed’s policy framework remained unclear.

## Real Yields and Inflation Compensation Drive the Treasury Selloff

Friday’s yield increases completed a punishing month for duration. The 2-year yield finished July 11.7 basis points higher, the 5-year rose 22.3 basis points, the 10-year climbed 27 basis points and the 30-year increased 32.1 basis points. The 2s30s spread widened 20.4 basis points during the month, showing that the adjustment went well beyond the timing of the next policy increase.

The 10-year real yield accounted for 22.4 basis points of the monthly rise in the nominal benchmark. Breakeven inflation increased only 4.6 basis points over the same period, but its contribution became more important on Friday as oil rebounded and policymakers emphasized the risk that inflation could remain above target. The result was a simultaneous increase in the real cost of capital and the compensation required for future inflation, rather than a simple substitution between the two.

Bond-index performance showed the consequence across maturities. The ICE U.S. Government 1–3 Year Bond Index slipped 0.04% on Friday and remained up 0.17% for July. The 7–10 Year index fell 0.31% on the day and 1.17% for the month, while the 20-plus-year index lost 0.69% on Friday and 3.87% in July. Long high-grade corporate indices declined more than 4% during the month, largely reflecting their duration exposure as government yields rose.

Trading activity was unusually heavy at month-end. FINRA recorded $1.92 trillion of Treasury par activity, 32.4% more than Thursday, across 577,862 trades. Nominal-coupon activity rose 33.4% to $1.52 trillion. Activity in coupons longer than 7 years through 10 years increased 56.4% to $279 billion, while turnover in maturities longer than 5 years through 7 years rose 88.5% to $173 billion. TIPS activity almost tripled to $121.2 billion. Those totals capture the scale and location of the adjustment without identifying which side of the market initiated it.

The late session supplied one counterforce. Treasury losses were pared around the 4 p.m. New York rebalancing of bond indices, when index-tracking funds incorporated debt issued during July. That demand did not reverse the day’s selloff or the monthly loss. The Bloomberg Treasury Index was already down nearly 0.9% for July through the previous session, with the Fed decision and earlier oil-driven repricing accounting for the month’s largest setbacks.

The Employment Cost Index added a domestic inflation concern distinct from energy. Its 0.9% quarterly increase exceeded the median forecast, indicating that labor costs had not slowed enough to reassure a market already questioning whether the policy rate was restrictive. The release did not establish an acceleration by itself, but Friday’s setting made even a small upside surprise consequential. As rates trader Tony Farren put it, the market required lower inflation evidence rather than another result that was marginally firmer than expected.

Oil then widened the range of possible outcomes. WTI settled above $84 at a one-week high as renewed U.S.-Iran fighting and threats to regional shipping kept supply risk elevated. The increase fed directly into longer maturities, where investors were already demanding more protection against inflation persisting through successive supply shocks.

The cross-asset response showed that higher yields did not arise from stronger risk appetite alone. The S&P 500 advanced almost 1% intraday before closing 0.70% higher, helped by Amazon and other large technology companies. Yet the semiconductor index’s negligible gain left it down 4.30% for the week and more than 20% for July. Investors were still differentiating sharply between companies able to fund the AI buildout and those most exposed to leverage, capacity expansion or crowded positioning.

The dollar’s weakness was more unusual. Bloomberg’s broad dollar gauge lost 1.3% over the week, its worst performance in more than three months, despite higher Treasury yields. Positioning had become heavily bullish before the Fed meeting: noncommercial traders held $49.23 billion of net dollar longs through July 28, the largest such position since 2014. The subsequent decline reflected both yen intervention and concern that the Fed’s reliance on market tightening could leave inflation insufficiently controlled.

## Fed Dissenters Define a Reaction Function the Chair Left Open

The three July dissenters supplied the clearest policy guidance of the week. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan had all voted to raise the federal-funds target from its 3.5%–3.75% range rather than leave it unchanged for a fifth consecutive meeting. Their Friday statements showed agreement on the direction of policy but important differences in emphasis.

Hammack said elevated inflation had persisted too long and argued that existing policy was not appropriately restrictive. She was not confident that inflation would return to 2% without additional action and saw demand pressure alongside the supply shocks that had lifted prices. Her argument treated the economy’s underlying strength as a reason to act while the cost of doing so remained manageable.

Kashkari favored a series of small increases rather than waiting until entrenched inflation required a larger intervention. He argued that the Fed could slow or pause subsequent adjustments if inflation receded, preserving flexibility while reducing the risk that continued delay would validate higher price expectations. That preference linked the size of each move to the uncertainty of the outlook rather than to a weaker commitment to tightening.

Logan said inflation appeared to be moving toward the mid-2% range rather than all the way to the Fed’s goal, even after accounting for productivity improvements and supply disturbances. She pointed to firm employment, spending and financial conditions as evidence that policy was not meaningfully restraining demand. In her assessment, a modest near-term increase would lower the probability of having to tighten more abruptly later.

Musalem, who does not currently vote, added that the bond-market selloff had made the Fed’s credibility dependent on higher rates and said he would have preferred a quarter-point move. Barkin, another nonvoter this year, stopped short of endorsing the dissenters but said it was a close question whether the existing rate was high enough to reduce inflation. He saw a case for reversing some of the cuts made in 2025.

These interventions changed the policy debate because they came from separately timed, named officials rather than an anonymous tightening faction. They also followed Chair Kevin Warsh’s decision not to specify what would trigger action. Warsh had argued that higher market yields were already tightening financial conditions and could perform part of the central bank’s work. The dissenters instead emphasized the risk that market restraint would not return inflation to target unless it was backed by policy.

The distinction matters most at the long end. A rise in yields caused by confidence in eventual disinflation would tighten financial conditions while preserving the Fed’s credibility. A rise driven by higher term premiums, inflation expectations or uncertainty about the central bank’s response would impose higher borrowing costs without delivering the same anchor. Friday’s equal contribution from real yields and breakevens, coupled with a weaker dollar, left room for the second interpretation.

Warsh’s communication strategy is becoming part of that premium. He has sought to reduce forward guidance, shortened the policy statement and created task forces to reassess communications, economic data and balance-sheet policy. Investors accustomed to using the Fed’s stated reaction function to price future meetings are now being asked to infer it from data and market movements whose own causes may be ambiguous.

A further institutional change surfaced over the weekend. Warsh raised at the July meeting the possibility of reducing the number of rate-setting gatherings to six a year, with two additional meetings devoted to substantive economic topics. The FOMC has held eight scheduled policy meetings annually since the early 1980s, and no decision has been made. Officials also discussed aligning decisions more closely with major data releases.

Changing meeting frequency would not prevent the Fed from convening during emergencies, but fewer scheduled decisions could increase the importance of each data cycle and lengthen the intervals in which markets must operate without a policy response. The proposal fits Warsh’s broader effort to change how the central bank communicates. It also arrives when the absence of guidance is already increasing demand for protection against larger yield moves.

Options markets reflected that concern. The premium for puts over calls on long-dated Treasury contracts reached its highest since March. Investors used September options to hedge 10-year yields approaching 4.8% or 4.9% and 30-year yields reaching roughly 5.3% to 5.42%. A long-bond put position purchased after the Fed meeting for about $20 million had already appreciated sharply as the 30-year yield approached its strike area.

Treasury’s quarterly refunding adds a separate uncertainty. Auction sizes for the August-to-October quarter were expected to remain steady, but investors were alert to any guidance preparing the market for increases in 2027. With the 30-year yield already above 5.27%, a signal of greater future coupon supply could reinforce the term premium even if the Fed’s next move becomes clearer.

The Treasury was also exploring a potential change to funding-market operations. Officials asked primary dealers about investing part of the government’s cash in the roughly $13 trillion repo market. Treasury held about $966 billion in its account at the Fed, within a cash balance near $1 trillion. Lending some of that money through repo could smooth the effects of tax dates, auction settlements and changes in the cash balance on short-term funding.

Supporters said the program could reduce periodic strains and allow the Fed to operate with a somewhat smaller balance sheet. Treasury’s borrowing advisers were less convinced, judging in May that operational difficulties could outweigh modest returns. Estimated earnings ranged from zero to 2 basis points while bank reserves remained ample and 5 to 10 basis points in a scarcer-reserve environment. Dealer capacity was another constraint: large, irregular Treasury repo operations could occupy balance sheet that intermediaries could not keep unused indefinitely.

## The BOJ Holds as Coordinated Intervention Changes the Yen Risk

Japan combined a conventional rate hold with an extraordinary currency operation. The Bank of Japan kept its benchmark at 1%, as all 52 surveyed economists expected, after raising it in June to the highest level since 1995. The vote was 8-1, with Hajime Takata seeking a second consecutive increase.

Governor Kazuo Ueda’s message was moderately hawkish without committing the bank to September. He said underlying inflation was approaching the 2% target, requiring greater attention to upside risks, and indicated that the board would begin more intensive policy discussions at its next meeting. He also said the BOJ could accelerate the pace of increases if it concluded that financial conditions were too accommodative.

The updated outlook supported keeping future meetings live. The BOJ changed its balance-of-risks assessment for growth from tilted to the downside to balanced and projected 0.6% expansion in the current fiscal year. It lowered its principal inflation forecast to 2.5% from 2.8% because of government subsidies, while warning that underlying inflation could overshoot 2% and that yen weakness had become a more consequential source of price pressure.

Data released before the decision reinforced that concern. Tokyo consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 1.9% in July from a year earlier, above the 1.8% forecast. Inflation excluding both fresh food and energy was 2%, as was the overall rate. Processed-food prices increased 3.9%, housework consumables rose 5.3% and services inflation edged up to 1.2%. Industrial production grew 1.3% in June from May and 4.2% from a year earlier, while retail sales rose 0.5% annually but fell 4.1% on the month. Unemployment held at 2.5%, and the job-to-applicant ratio increased to 1.18 from 1.17.

The policy message was not forceful enough to sustain the yen’s initial intervention-driven surge. The currency had risen as much as 3.3% against the dollar during Thursday’s New York session after Japan entered the market, according to market participants. BOJ account projections indicated that the operation was approximately ¥8.45 trillion, or $52.8 billion, likely the largest single-day intervention by Tokyo.

The estimate came from an expected ¥8.2 trillion fiscal-related decline in the BOJ’s Monday current-account balance when money brokers had anticipated an increase. The Finance Ministry did not immediately confirm the operation, but the discrepancy made intervention highly likely. U.S. authorities also conducted rate checks, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described the yen as very undervalued and excessive volatility as unhealthy.

Action continued during Friday’s New York session. A person familiar with the matter said Japanese authorities again bought yen and sold dollars. At least two large U.S. banks were asked by the New York Fed to check the euro-yen rate, while separate reporting said the New York Fed sold euros for yen on behalf of the U.S. Treasury. The yen gained about 1.3% against the dollar on Friday and closed near 157.28, reversing more than two months of depreciation in two sessions.

The scale and bilateral nature of the operation changed the immediate risk for short-yen positions. Hedge funds had held 124,575 bearish-yen contracts, worth about $9.5 billion, as of July 28, close to the June peak and the largest short exposure since 2007. Intervention confronted that positioning with both direct purchases and the prospect that Washington would support further action.

The longer-term constraint remained the interest-rate differential. Japan’s 1% policy rate was far below the 3.75% upper bound of the U.S. range. Ueda opened the door to tightening but did not promise a move, and traders assigned about an 89% probability to an increase by October. The next BOJ decision is due Sept. 18, two days after the Fed’s scheduled meeting.

The weekend brought a formal escalation in coordination. Japan confirmed its first joint intervention with the U.S. in 15 years, while President Donald Trump called the action a signal of friendship and Bessent said Washington would not hesitate to intervene again. A photographed note in front of the Treasury secretary listed a plan to buy $5 billion to $10 billion of yen. Those confirmations occurred after Friday’s fixed-income close and therefore did not drive the Treasury session, but they increased the likelihood that any renewed yen decline would meet additional official resistance.

Coordination can buy time, but it does not resolve the policy and fiscal forces behind the currency’s weakness. Higher oil prices worsen Japan’s import bill, and the government’s spending plans have raised concern about debt issuance. Intervention may also require Japan to liquidate foreign securities, including Treasuries, creating a potential spillover into U.S. borrowing costs. The durability of the yen rebound therefore depends on whether BOJ tightening, Fed policy and Japan’s fiscal outlook begin to support the official operation.

## Europe’s Inflation Pickup and Colombia’s Pause Broaden the Policy Divide

Euro-area inflation accelerated to 2.9% in July from 2.8% in June, matching the median forecast but strengthening the case for another ECB increase. Energy prices rose 10% from a year earlier, while services inflation and the measure excluding food and energy also accelerated. German bonds gave up earlier gains, lifting the 10-year yield 1 basis point to 3.16%.

France delivered the largest national surprise. Inflation jumped to 2.4% from 2%, exceeding every estimate in the survey. Services inflation increased to 2.3% from 1.9%, and energy inflation reached 12.4%. The rise followed stronger-than-expected French output and similar inflation acceleration in Spain and Germany, reducing the case that the energy shock was being offset by weak demand.

Markets continued to assign about a 90% probability to a quarter-point ECB increase in September and priced 42 basis points of tightening by year-end. Austria’s Martin Kocher emphasized the unusually high uncertainty, Lithuania’s Gediminas Simkus said a hike was much more likely than a hold, and Slovakia’s Peter Kazimir argued that at least one further increase would be required even if conditions improved.

The ECB will receive August inflation and new staff projections before deciding. July’s report established that the energy impulse was broad enough to lift both the headline and underlying measures, but it did not settle how persistent the pass-through would be. Wage growth in an ECB survey was expected to accelerate through early 2027, while second-quarter output had expanded at twice the forecast pace and at its fastest rate in more than a year.

In Britain, BOE Chief Economist Huw Pill developed the hawkish case after voting with two colleagues for an increase. He warned that volatile energy and commodity prices could persist into 2027 because the duration and scale of the Iran conflict remained profoundly uncertain. The BOE’s central forecast put inflation at 3.2% at year-end, while an adverse scenario involving stronger energy costs and second-round effects produced inflation of 4.5% in 2027 and materially higher rates from the current 3.75%.

Pill’s concern was not merely the first-round increase in fuel. U.K. petrol prices reached 159.97 pence a liter, 20% above their prewar level, but the policy division centered on whether companies would raise prices and workers would demand compensation. Governor Andrew Bailey and five other committee members saw weak demand and a soft labor market limiting that process. Pill argued that policy should prevent self-sustaining effects rather than wait for them to become visible, although he acknowledged that inflation expectations had not substantially de-anchored.

Colombia provided a different response to above-target inflation. Its central bank unexpectedly held the policy rate at 12%, an outcome predicted by only four of 27 economists; the others expected increases of 25 to 75 basis points. Four board members supported the hold, while three wanted a half-point increase.

Governor Leonardo Villar described the decision as a pause rather than the end of the tightening cycle. Annual inflation remained above 6% against a 3% target with a 1-percentage-point tolerance band, but the peso had appreciated nearly 20% against the dollar during the year, reducing imported-price pressure. The central bank also announced a program to accumulate as much as $4 billion of international reserves, a measure that could temper the currency’s strength.

The policy setting remained politically and fiscally difficult. Expansionary government spending, a 23% minimum-wage increase and temporary food and energy shocks were all contributing to inflation. The independent fiscal committee expected the budget deficit to exceed 7% of GDP. Villar said rate increases remained possible, and the September meeting will include a new finance minister after President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella takes office on Aug. 7.

## Credit Stress Separates Duration Losses From Borrower-Specific Risk

The rise in government yields continued to pressure municipal bonds even without a broad deterioration in issuer credit. The Bloomberg Municipal Bond Index had lost 1.72% through Thursday, its worst July since 2003 and only its second negative month of the year. Approximately $47 billion of issuance arrived during a month that normally benefits from lower supply and reinvestment of coupon payments and redemptions.

The unusual combination of heavy issuance and rising Treasury yields overwhelmed those seasonal supports. Municipal securities consequently cheapened relative to Treasuries, but portfolio managers attributed the move mainly to the higher-rate environment rather than worsening state and local finances. That distinction did not remove duration losses; it identified the repricing as a market-wide cost-of-capital adjustment rather than evidence of a generalized credit event.

New York City illustrated the difference between near-term market access and a deteriorating medium-term fiscal path. Fitch and Moody’s kept their ratings unchanged but maintained negative outlooks on the city’s $53 billion of general-obligation debt before a planned $1.5 billion bond offering. Moody’s rated the debt Aa2 and Fitch AA.

The city balanced a $126 billion budget without drawing reserves or increasing property taxes, helped by tax collections that exceeded forecasts by $4.3 billion in the fiscal year through June. Yet the spending plan was $10 billion larger than the previous year’s and relied on temporary measures, including a longer schedule for paying pension obligations and additional state support. Projected deficits widen to $6.4 billion in fiscal 2028 and $8.5 billion in 2030. The agencies said recurring gap-closing measures would determine whether the ratings remained intact over the coming year.

Northwell Healthcare added as much as $800 million of potential supply to the New York municipal pipeline. The health system expected tax-exempt issuance through the Dormitory Authority of the State of New York, with Jefferies as bookrunner, but had not determined structure, maturity or timing. Hospitals had already issued about $26.7 billion of municipal bonds during the year.

Stress was more acute in lower-quality corporate structures. Cable One creditors began organizing as a selloff in the broadband company’s debt threatened approximately $1 billion of new financing. The company needs the funds for a mandatory acquisition of the remaining 55% of Mega Broadband Investments after private-equity owner GTCR exercised a put option.

Financing discussions had centered on a yield near 12%, already among the highest for a transaction this year. Prospective lenders wanted strict ring-fencing to prevent Cable One from using parent resources to support Mega Broadband’s heavier debt burden. As existing Cable One debt deteriorated, some first-lien loans traded at yields approaching 18%, raising the possibility that a new package would be too expensive to complete. Cable One had at least $3 billion of long-term debt at March 31, along with high leverage, constrained free cash flow and intense residential-broadband competition.

Extenet Systems had moved from refinancing pressure to payment failure. The miniature-cell-tower operator missed interest due July 27 on asset-backed securities, placing the bonds in default. Midland Loan Services, the PNC Bank division responsible for collections, also alleged that funds belonging to bondholders had been deposited into other accounts and that some liens had ceased to be perfected.

The company had issued about $500 million of asset-backed securities and warned creditors in June that it was close to running out of cash. Moody’s said Extenet was negotiating an interest-forbearance agreement, while Kroll continued to seek information. The cash-management allegations made the problem more serious than an operating shortfall alone because they raised questions about the controls intended to protect securitized creditors.

The contrast between Cable One and Extenet marked two stages of the same funding constraint. Cable One still had prospective access but faced double-digit yields, ring-fencing demands and competing creditor groups. Extenet had already missed payment and was negotiating forbearance amid alleged violations of its transaction documents. Neither case established a broad shutdown in credit, but both showed how higher risk-free rates and weaker operating performance expose structures that previously depended on inexpensive refinancing.

Romania’s sovereign rating supplied another example of access preserved under warning. Fitch affirmed the country at BBB-, its lowest investment-grade rating, with a negative outlook after the government appealed the agency’s initial decision and provided additional information. The announcement came after Friday’s U.S. close and did not contribute to the Treasury move.

Romania’s deficit was expected to fall below 6% of GDP this year from more than 9% in 2024, but the government had operated without a parliamentary majority since its coalition collapsed in May. Fitch cited uncertainty about the composition and stability of the next administration and reduced visibility over fiscal strategy after 2026. Moody’s is scheduled to review the rating on Aug. 7, while two further reforms require approval by the end of August to unlock additional European Union recovery money.

## Forward Market Significance

The July employment report on Aug. 7 is the first major U.S. test after the dissenters defined their case for immediate tightening. Economists expect payrolls to increase by 85,000 after a 57,000 gain in June, with unemployment holding at 4.2%. A stronger result would reinforce the view that policy is not restraining demand enough to return inflation to target. A weak report would reopen the question of whether the Fed should respond to energy-led inflation when labor demand is losing momentum.

The surrounding labor indicators will help establish breadth. Job openings are due Tuesday, ADP’s estimate of private employment Wednesday and jobless claims Thursday. Separately timed speeches from Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid, Governor Lisa Cook and Musalem will show whether support for the dissenters is extending beyond the officials who favored a July increase.

The Treasury’s August-to-October refunding announcement is a distinct duration event. Auction sizes are expected to remain unchanged, but the market will focus on whether officials preserve or soften guidance that increases remain distant. With 10-year option structures targeting yields near 4.9% and long-bond hedges extending toward 5.42%, an earlier signal of larger 2027 supply could prolong the selloff even if the employment data settle the September policy debate.

Fed communication itself remains a source of volatility. Reports that Warsh is considering six rate-setting meetings a year add an institutional question to uncertainty over the inflation framework and the role of market yields in policy. Any clarification of the proposal, the scheduling of data-dependent decisions or the conditions for a September increase would affect how much premium investors require between meetings.

The yen will test whether coordinated intervention can survive without immediate reinforcement from rate differentials. The Sept. 16 Fed decision and Sept. 18 BOJ meeting place the two policy paths in close succession. Renewed depreciation toward the levels that triggered last week’s action would test the U.S. and Japanese commitment to intervene again; sustained stability would give Ueda more room to evaluate inflation and the effects of June’s increase.

For the ECB, August inflation and staff forecasts must determine whether July’s 10% rise in energy costs is spreading into services and wages. France’s 2.4% inflation surprise and the euro area’s 2.9% result support a September increase, but officials still need to judge whether the shock will persist as growth absorbs higher energy costs.

In credit, Cable One’s financing terms will show whether a 12% yield and enforceable ring-fencing can still attract sufficient demand for a mandatory acquisition. Extenet’s forbearance talks will test whether bondholders can restore cash controls and lien protection after the payment default. New York City’s $1.5 billion offering will provide a cleaner measure of how municipal investors distinguish high Treasury yields from an issuer’s medium-term budget risks.

Oil remains the common variable across these tests. Another interruption to Gulf shipping or escalation in U.S.-Iran fighting would challenge the assumption that the energy shock is temporary, strengthen the Fed and ECB dissenters’ arguments and keep breakevens elevated. A durable improvement in shipping and diplomacy could relieve inflation compensation, but the July close showed that long Treasuries also require confidence in real-rate policy, fiscal supply and the central bank’s reaction function before the broader duration premium can recede.

section_summaries.summary: July’s duration losses deepened as the 10-year yield rose 27 basis points and the 30-year climbed 32.1 basis points over the month. The 10-year real yield accounted for 22.4 basis points of the nominal benchmark’s increase, while breakevens became more influential on Friday as oil rebounded. Heavy month-end trading and index demand pared late losses but did not reverse the selloff.

section_summaries.summary: Hammack, Kashkari and Logan agreed that rates should rise but differed on the reasoning and pace, ranging from insufficient restraint to incremental increases that preserve flexibility. Their arguments challenged Chair Kevin Warsh’s reliance on higher market yields to do part of the Fed’s work. Possible changes to meeting frequency, uncertainty over future Treasury supply and heavier long-end option hedging added to the premium around policy and duration.

section_summaries.section_title: The BOJ Holds as Coordinated Intervention Changes the Yen Risk
section_summaries.summary: The BOJ kept its policy rate at 1% in an 8-1 vote while Ueda signaled closer attention to upside inflation risks without committing to September. Japanese yen purchases, U.S. rate checks and reported U.S. Treasury involvement confronted crowded short-yen positions with coordinated official resistance. The currency rebounded sharply, but the wide U.S.-Japan rate gap and Japan’s fiscal and energy pressures still limit the durability of that move.

section_summaries.next_check: August inflation and new ECB forecasts will test whether the energy shock is spreading into services and wages.
section_summaries.section_title: Europe’s Inflation Pickup and Colombia’s Pause Broaden the Policy Divide
section_summaries.summary: Euro-area inflation accelerated to 2.9%, with stronger energy, services and core readings supporting expectations for another ECB increase. BOE Chief Economist Huw Pill argued that persistent energy costs could produce second-round effects even as most colleagues emphasized weak demand. Colombia unexpectedly held its rate at 12%, treating the decision as a pause while peso appreciation reduced imported-price pressure despite inflation above 6%.

section_summaries.market_read: Higher risk-free rates are exposing borrowers and structures that depended on inexpensive refinancing.
section_summaries.next_check: Cable One’s financing and Extenet’s forbearance will test whether creditor protections can preserve access or recover value.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Stress Separates Duration Losses From Borrower-Specific Risk
section_summaries.summary: Municipal losses largely reflected rising Treasury yields and heavy issuance rather than broad issuer deterioration, although New York City’s negative outlooks highlighted medium-term budget risk. Cable One still had prospective financing access but faced yields near 12%, ring-fencing demands and weakening debt prices. Extenet had progressed to payment default and forbearance talks amid allegations involving cash controls and liens.

The next tests separate policy, supply and inflation risks: U.S. labor data will challenge the dissenters’ case, Treasury refunding guidance will shape the term premium, and oil disruptions could keep breakevens elevated. Fed communication, coordinated yen intervention, European inflation persistence and stressed-credit negotiations remain additional channels through which the repricing can extend.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as labor costs, hawkish Fed dissent and oil lift real yields and inflation compensation
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended July with a broad selloff. The 2-year yield rose 4.5 basis points to 4.292%, the 5-year and 10-year each climbed 6.2 basis points to 4.45% and 4.736%, and the 30-year increased 5.9 basis points to 5.274%. At 10 years, the real yield rose 3.6 basis points and breakeven inflation increased 2.6 basis points, showing that higher real borrowing costs and inflation compensation contributed almost equally.

The Q2 Employment Cost Index rose 0.9%, slightly above expectations, while Fed voters Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari and Lorie Logan explained why they had favored an immediate rate increase in July. Oil added to the inflation concern as unresolved supply threats lifted WTI and Brent and capped monthly gains above 20%.

The decline in bonds was not a broad flight from risk: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 advanced, while the dollar weakened despite higher U.S. yields. Japan’s intervention and the BOJ’s moderately hawkish hold also altered yen risk, but the large U.S.-Japan rate gap remained a constraint on the currency’s rebound.
